proposals.impact: convert 4 stuck intro-screen sessions into quiz starts
proposals.observation: All 4 quiz sessions in the 48-hour window loaded the intro screen and went no further. Zero starts, zero completions. Every visitor who arrived — two direct, two from Instagram — stopped at the same point. The intro screen is the only confirmed friction point in the data. No other step was reached by anyone.
proposals.proposal: The intro screen is doing something that makes four separate people decide not to begin. The most common culprit at this stage is either a vague value proposition ("find out your money type") that doesn't earn the click, or a time-commitment signal that feels too heavy. Rewrite the intro headline and sub-copy to name a specific, felt experience the ICP already has — not a promise about what the quiz will deliver. Ground it in the £150k story or the unopened-tab moment so it reads as Joel's voice, not quiz-template copy. Keep the CTA button text direct and low-stakes.

proposals.impact: lift Money Worship open rate from 37.5% toward Vigilance's 66.7%
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation opens at 66.67% against 12 sends. Money Avoidance opens at 52.63% against 19 sends. Money Worship opens at 37.5% against 16 sends — the weakest of the three by a clear margin. All three automations run on the same list logic, so the gap is almost certainly in the subject line or preview text of the first Money Worship email, not in list quality or send timing.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line and preview text of the first Money Worship automation email. The current subject is not in the data, but the open-rate gap tells you it isn't earning the open the way the Vigilance subject does. Money Worship subscribers have just been told they tie their self-worth to income or possessions — they are primed for recognition, not challenge. A subject line that mirrors that specific felt state (the month you earn well and still feel empty, the pay rise that didn't fix anything) will outperform a generic "your results" framing. Apply the Sultanic test: write something only Joel could write about what Money Worship actually feels like from the inside.

proposals.impact: restore failed workflow so competitive intel resumes flowing
proposals.observation: The Funnel-Hack Digest workflow failed at 10:47 on 31 May with a conclusion of "failure". It is the only failed workflow in 19 runs. The workflow name suggests it pulls competitive or market intelligence that feeds Joel's content or positioning decisions. A silent failure means that feed has been dark since this morning with no alert actioned.
proposals.proposal: Add a failure notification step to the Funnel-Hack Digest workflow so any future failure surfaces immediately rather than sitting in the CI log until Fred's next audit catches it. The fix is a single `on-failure` step at the end of the job that posts to wherever Joel already receives alerts — Slack, email, or a GitHub issue. Given the workflow file is in the blocked path list, this proposal is flagged medium risk: Joel must apply the diff manually rather than Fred committing it. The observation stands regardless. The current job silently swallows failures.
proposals.current_text:
- name: Run digest scraper
        run: node scripts/funnel-hack-digest.js
proposals.new_text:
- name: Run digest scraper
        run: node scripts/funnel-hack-digest.js

      - name: Notify on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            await github.rest.issues.create({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              title: "Funnel-Hack Digest failed — " + new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10),
              body: "The Funnel-Hack Digest workflow failed. Check the run at: " + context.serverUrl + "/" + context.repo.owner + "/" + context.repo.repo + "/actions/runs/" + context.runId,
              labels: ["ci-failure"]
            })
